prompts.residents: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent production sprite atlas for ORDRE DE CENDRE (Imperium March), original military-industrial science-fiction side-scrolling game. Painterly semi-realistic character art matching salt-weathered maritime workers, realistic human proportions, restrained petrol teal, muted sage, weathered cream and ochre clothing, fine matte textile detail, clear silhouettes, diffuse light from upper left. Strict orthographic full-body SIDE VIEW facing RIGHT in every upright pose, level camera with no perspective tilt. True PNG alpha transparency outside all silhouettes, no ground or cast shadow. No text, labels, digits, captions, logos, medical crosses, grid lines, scenery, floating props, weapons, blood or watermark. Every figure wholly contained in its cell, at least 25 transparent pixels clear around it, absolutely no clipped boots, heads, hands or luggage. Maintain identical costume and identity across each pose sequence. Natural adult body proportions and consistent human scale between cells. Lying poses retain the same scale as standing and fit horizontally inside their cell. Compose exactly TWELVE sprites in a strict 4 columns by 3 rows equal-cell grid, landscape 4:3 sheet. FIRST SIX cells in reading order are resident A: adult woman with medium brown skin, dark hair tied in a low bun, faded ochre raincoat, cream scarf, dark teal trousers, rubber boots, small practical cloth satchel across body. LAST SIX cells in reading order are resident B: older adult man with light skin, short gray hair and short beard, faded sage knitted cap, worn dark petrol work jacket, cream shirt collar, brown trousers, rubber boots, small waist utility pouch. These are civilian residents of the Nacre waterworks neighborhood, not soldiers, not medical staff. For EACH six-cell person in order: 1 standing relaxed idle, 2 walking contact with right leg forward, 3 walking passing with rear leg swinging under body, 4 walking opposite contact with left leg forward, 5 walking opposite passing, 6 lying still on their side, non-graphic closed eyes and relaxed hands, no wounds. Thus row1 contains A idle and first three walking poses; row2 A final walking pose, A lying pose, B idle, B first walking pose; row3 B remaining three walking poses then B lying pose. Keep silhouette and scale coherent, adult heads same size in every cell.
